`final class Color`<br/>
**Extends:** [`LockableValue<Color>`](/reference/utilities/lockablevalue/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.color` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [Color.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/color/Color.java)

An RGBA color with channels on 1, which can also hold a linear gradient or change on every frame.

## Description

Every color setter of JOID takes a `Color`.
Create one from a hex string, from channels, or take a named constant:

```java fragment
final Color text = Color.decode("#E7E9EE");
final Color shadow = new Color(0F, 0F, 0F, 0.6F);
final Color glow = Color.decode("#5B8CFF").toGradient(Color.decode("#7DA4FF"));
```

An animated color, such as [`Color.RAINBOW`](/reference/drawing/color/#Color-factory-RAINBOW), carries an update function that JOID applies each time it draws the color.
Two colors are equal when their channels, their gradient and their update function are equal; the update function compares by identity.

## Creation details

<a id="Color-factory-rgb"></a>

### rgb

`Color rgb(int value)` <span class="joid-qualifier">factory</span>

Creates an opaque color from a packed `0xRRGGBB` value; the top byte is ignored.

<a id="Color-factory-argb"></a>

### argb

`Color argb(int value)` <span class="joid-qualifier">factory</span>

Creates a color from a packed `0xAARRGGBB` value, alpha in the top byte.

<a id="Color-factory-decode"></a>

### decode

`Color decode(String nm)` <span class="joid-qualifier">factory</span>

**Throws:**

- `NumberFormatException`: The color … cannot be decoded, write it as #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA, rgb(r, g, b), rgba(r, g, b, a) or gradient(from, to)

Parses a color from text, with or without `#`: `#RRGGBB` (opaque), `#RRGGBBAA` (alpha last), `rgb(r, g, b)` with channels from 0 to 255, `rgba(r, g, b, a)` with an alpha on 1, `gradient(from, to)` for a left-to-right gradient or `gradient(from, to, x1, y1, x2, y2)` with a direction (see `toGradient`), and `rainbow` or `loading` for a copy of the animated constants.
Throws `NumberFormatException` for any other text.

<a id="Color-factory-RAINBOW"></a>

### RAINBOW

`Color RAINBOW()` <span class="joid-qualifier">factory</span>

Returns the color of the rainbow cycle at this instant of the JOID clock: a full turn of hues every 3 seconds.
The result is a plain color that does not change: pass the constant [`Color.RAINBOW`](/reference/drawing/color/#Color-factory-RAINBOW) to a setter instead, so that the color cycles by itself.

`Color RAINBOW(long time)` <span class="joid-qualifier">factory</span>

Returns the color of the rainbow cycle at `time`, in milliseconds of the JOID clock.

<a id="Color-factory-LOADING"></a>

### LOADING

`Color LOADING()` <span class="joid-qualifier">factory</span>

Returns the color of the loading pulse at this instant: a dark gray that brightens and darkens slightly, one cycle every 2 seconds.
The result is a plain color: pass the constant [`Color.LOADING`](/reference/drawing/color/#Color-factory-LOADING) to a setter instead, so that the color pulses by itself.

<a id="Color-constructor"></a>

### Color

`Color(FloatBuffer buffer)` 

Reads red, green, blue and alpha on 1 from the current position of the buffer, which advances by four floats.

`Color(java.awt.Color color)` 

Converts a `java.awt.Color`.

`Color(ColorGradient gradient)` 

Creates a gradient color from a [`ColorGradient`](/reference/drawing/colorgradient/); its own channels are those of the start color.

`Color(int r, int g, int b)` 

Creates an opaque color from red, green and blue from 0 to 255.

`Color(float r, float g, float b)` 

Creates an opaque color from red, green and blue on 1.

`Color(int r, int g, int b, int a)` 

Creates a color from red, green, blue and alpha from 0 to 255.

`Color(float r, float g, float b, float a)` 

Creates a color from red, green, blue and alpha on 1.
Every channel is clamped between `0F` and `1F`.

`Color(float r, float g, float b, float a, UnaryOperator<Color> update)` 

Creates an animated color: each time JOID draws it, JOID passes this color to `update` and draws the color that it returns.
A channel that you set later with `red`, `green`, `blue` or `alpha` overrides that channel on every frame.

## Property details

<a id="Color-property-red"></a>

### red

- `this red(float red)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>
- `int getRed()` 

**Default:** set at creation

The red channel: `getRed()` reads it from 0 to 255, `getRedF()` on 1.
`red(float)` sets it in place, on 1, and throws `IllegalStateException` on a locked color such as a named constant.

## Method details

<a id="Color-method-bind"></a>

### bind

`void bind()` 

Sets the color of the render state to the current frame of this color.
Draws without a color of their own, such as images and [`Tessellator`](/reference/drawing/tessellator/) batches without vertex colors, are tinted by it.

`void bind(Runnable runnable, BoundingBox canvas)` 

Runs `runnable` with this color applied, then restores the previous color of the render state.
For a gradient, it binds the gradient shader instead, spread over `canvas` in the coordinates you draw in.

`void bind(Runnable runnable, BoundingBox canvas, boolean hasTexture)` 

Same as `bind(Runnable, BoundingBox)`; if `hasTexture` is `true`, a gradient multiplies the bound texture instead of replacing it, which tints an image.

<a id="Color-method-to"></a>

### to

`this to(Color target, float progress)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Returns the color between this one and `target` at `progress` on 1: `0F` gives a copy of this color, `1F` a copy of `target`, alpha included.
Two gradients blend stop by stop and point by point; a plain color blends with each stop of a gradient.
When either side is animated, the result is animated and blends the current frame of both sides.

<a id="Color-method-toGradient"></a>

### toGradient

`this toGradient(Color target)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Returns a left-to-right gradient from this color to `target`.

`Color toGradient(Color target, Point startPoint, Point endPoint)` 

Returns a gradient from this color to `target` along the line from `startPoint` to `endPoint`.
The points are on 1 of the drawn area: `(0, 0)` is its top-left corner and `(1, 1)` its bottom-right corner, so `(0, 0)` to `(0, 1)` runs from top to bottom.

Opaque light pink: red `1F`, green and blue `0.7F`.

<a id="Color-constant-WHITE"></a>

### WHITE

`Color WHITE` 

Opaque white, `#FFFFFFFF`.

<a id="Color-constant-GREEN"></a>

### GREEN

`Color GREEN` 

Opaque green, `#00FF00FF`.

<a id="Color-constant-BLACK"></a>

### BLACK

`Color BLACK` 

Opaque black, `#000000FF`.

<a id="Color-constant-YELLOW"></a>

### YELLOW

`Color YELLOW` 

Opaque yellow, `#FFFF00FF`.

<a id="Color-constant-ORANGE"></a>

### ORANGE

`Color ORANGE` 

Opaque orange: red `1F`, green `0.5F`, blue `0F`.

<a id="Color-constant-MAGENTA"></a>

### MAGENTA

`Color MAGENTA` 

Opaque magenta, `#FF00FFFF`.

<a id="Color-constant-DARKGRAY"></a>

### DARKGRAY

`Color DARKGRAY` 

Opaque dark gray, `0.3F` on every channel.

<a id="Color-constant-LIGHTGRAY"></a>

### LIGHTGRAY

`Color LIGHTGRAY` 

Opaque light gray, `0.7F` on every channel.

<a id="Color-constant-TRANSPARENT"></a>

### TRANSPARENT

`Color TRANSPARENT` 

Fully transparent black: draws nothing.

<a id="Color-constant-RAINBOW"></a>

### RAINBOW

`Color RAINBOW` 

An animated color that cycles through the hues every 3 seconds, at 80 % saturation and brightness; its alpha is kept.

<a id="Color-constant-LOADING"></a>

### LOADING

`Color LOADING` 

An animated color that pulses slightly around a dark gray every 2 seconds, the look of a loading placeholder; its alpha is kept.

---

<small>`fluent` returns the instance, typed for chaining · `factory` creates an instance · `signal` also accepts a value that follows signals, as a signal, an expression or a lambda ([When does JOID compute this value again?](/use/learn/interactivity/signals/#ask-when-does-joid-compute-this-value-again)) · `hook` called by JOID, override it · `abstract` you implement it · `default` interface method with a body · `static` called on the class · `protected` visible to subclasses</small>
